parsed.explanation: The combined regime couples a national universal-exposure document regime (passports forced to birth sex, X markers ended, visa officers instructed to refuse on 'reasonable doubt' about sex with potential lifetime fraud findings, documented strandings) with a division that is the country's worst: the highest per-capita killing rate of trans women (24.7/100k, an undercount floor), a 2026 mob beating whose victims were charged while no attacker was arrested, one victim denied hospital care and placed in a men's jail and searched by a male guard despite a female licence marker, a 2024 prison killing, no state gender-identity hate-crime coverage, surgical-proof marker rules, a minors' care ban, and one of the country's most severe municipal restroom ordinances. Severity is lethal and state-implicated; frequency is the highest documented in the nation. No execution pathway or routine visitor imprisonment is documented, keeping it above the 0.05–0.15 anchors, but state tolerance of lethal violence plus universal document exposure sit firmly in Severe Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports must show sex assigned at birth; X markers stopped; visa cable directs refusal where documents cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscations and strandings; allied governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Ongoing court challenge to passport policy; civil-liberties suit; existing X passports valid until expiry; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening fraud finding can escalate to permanent inadmissibility; document mismatch feeds later police, hospital and custody encounters in the division.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Mob-attack victim jailed in men's facility, searched by male guard despite female licence marker; hospital care denied; national corrections policies mandate hair-cutting, hormone withdrawal, 'conversion' psychiatric therapy; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse; 2024 prison killing of a trans woman.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any police contact (restroom ordinance, 'disturbing the peace' charges) routes into birth-sex custody placement; national and state custody regimes compound.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No statewide facilities statute established for this division, but a municipality passed one of the country's most severe restroom ordinances; national order bars gender-congruent facilities in federally funded single-sex settings; 4 states criminalise in certain circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Most states lack bans; court injunctions against some national measures.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Restroom use triggers municipal ordinance enforcement, mob violence, victim-charging and men's-jail placement, as the August 2026 case shows.

care_services.exposure: Minors' care banned since Jan 2024 (veto overridden); transition care excluded from insurance and public coverage; national subpoenas of hospital records for under-19 patients; national insurance reimbursement ban proposed.
care_services.interaction: A travelling trans minor cannot access care; a guardian seeking care risks record exposure via hospital subpoenas; emergency care denied in the documented custody case.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 'radical gender ideology' framing in reward memo; state charges victims of mob violence while recording no attacker arrests; school-transition facilitation prosecuted; state sodomy statute (unenforced, 5 years + registry) remains.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute (2009) as residual recourse; state statute excludes gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police treatment of victims as offenders converts street violence into state exposure; national framing raises surveillance and discovery probability.

minors_guardians.exposure: State ban on puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for minors; national directive to prosecute facilitators of social transition; school sports barred; hospital record subpoenas reach minors' records.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and potential investigation or record exposure; school-related rules apply to visiting minors in state schools.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Highest per-capita trans-woman killing rate nationally (24.7/100k, undercount floor, worst-law states highest); August 2026 mob beating with victims charged, no arrests, one denied care and men's-jail placement; lethal prison violence 2024.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute nominally available; national employment-discrimination ruling as residual recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response (charging victims, impunity) is itself the exposure; resting on the national hate-crime statute is thin where bias crimes fall to federal prosecution.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: State has no gender-identity anti-discrimination law; marker changes require surgical proof; killing counts are unreliable undercounts; municipal ordinance scope and statewide restroom position unresolved; pending targeting bills may worsen rules.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Two municipalities protect gender identity; national litigation may enjoin passport and other orders; hate-crime statute exists nationally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are remote, partial and untested for visitors; unresolved litigation means operative rules can shift between booking and arrival.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similarities: state-tolerated lethal violence, birth-sex custody with abuse, impunity, and a latent morality statute. This jurisdiction documents fewer routine arrests of visitors than 0.15-E's hotel-reporting arrests, but its killing rate is the nation's highest and victims are prosecuted — materially comparable severity, slightly less routine custodial capture of visitors, so just above the 0.15 cluster.

0.25-C features birth-sex prison placement and a cross-dressing arrest statute with brief sentences. This jurisdiction matches the custody placement (male guard, men's jail) but adds the country's highest trans-woman killing rate, victim-charging, denied hospital care, and a national universal document/fraud regime — a worse tier on multiple axes, so clearly below 0.25-C.

0.35-A's register produces exclusion and humiliation without lethal outcomes. This jurisdiction's national document regime is a comparable universal exposure, but the division adds lethal violence at the nation's highest rate, state-implicated impunity, and harmful custody — a materially worse consequence profile, placing it well below 0.35-A.

0.75-C allows entry on matching markers, trained officers, and working tribunals with release after brief detention. Here markers cannot match by national design, custody places by birth sex, and attacks end with victims charged — the opposite of 0.75-C's protective, remedied regime; the gap to 0.75 is the largest on the scale examined.

parsed.synthesis: The national layer creates unavoidable exposure for every trans visitor: identity documents that by policy cannot reflect identity, visa adjudication instructions that convert presentation-mismatch into refusal or a lifetime fraud finding, and documented strandings — a tier-1 universal measure. The division layer converts any outing into the most dangerous documented environment in the country: lethal violence at the highest per-capita rate, mob attacks where police charge the victims, denial of hospital care, men's-facility custody and male-guard searches despite a female marker, no state gender-identity hate-crime coverage, surgical-proof document rules, and a minors' care ban that exposes travelling families. Documented protections (national hate-crime statute, employment ruling, marriage recognition, pending litigation, municipal ordinances) are resident-facing or unproven for visitors and do not offset operative exposures. State implication in impunity plus universal document exposure yields Severe Risk: 0.18.
